assumptions: Profile caepipe-mbf-si-pilot-1: MBF version 15.10, OPTIONS SI with the default vertical axis Y; SWBPIPE global X, Y, Z are written unchanged as the target program's X, Y, Z, with gravity along -Y. The writer always writes Y vertical: SWBPIPE has one vertical convention (weight along -Y) and the model document records no vertical axis, so a Z-vertical import, which arrives rotated, is written Y-vertical.

Lengths are written in mm, forces in N, moments in N*m, modulus in N/mm2 (= MPa), temperatures in C; SI source units scale to these by an exact power of ten, and US-customary units by the exact definitions listed in MBF-SI-UNITS-NORMALIZED (Design caepipe-mbf-import.md section 5.2).
Load case mapping: mechanical cases (concentrated force, concentrated moment, weight) -> 'Sustained (W+P)'; thermal and imposed-displacement cases -> 'Expansion (T1)'.
Materials are written temperature-independent: identical E and expansion coefficient at 20 C, 120 C; the optional allowable, yield and rupture columns are omitted.

Every LOADS entry has Pressure 1 = the element's pressure-region pressure in the sustained case, in bar (1 bar = 1e5 Pa exactly; psi by its exact definition), or 0 outside every region and specific gravity 0 (empty pipe); Temperature 1 = reference temperature + the element's SWBPIPE thermal change (summed when several primitives act on one element).

Piping code B311-80, chosen by the caller, is written in OPTIONS; OPCODE is written 0,0,0: axial force in the code stress off and liberal allowable off (code-stress settings only), and B31J off, so SIFs and flexibility factors come from the code's own appendix and a tee assembles no branch flexibility (Analysis; Format of .MBF, OPCODE). Every bend carries the user flexibility factor, which replaces the code's value (Bend).

OPPRES is written 0,0,0,1,0: field 1 = 0, the pressure-stress option CAEPIPE's public User's Manual defines as PD/4t (Appendix A, OPPRES); a piping code may fix the formula instead (OPCODE). Bourdon effect off, pressure correction for bends off, peak pressure factor 1. SWBPIPE's exact pressure route models neither effect (DEL-04-07 D-3).
The pressure contract, region ids, members, terminals with their closure transfer and the provenance are not in the MBF; the sidecar's pressure_map carries them for a bound import.

Weight per length w (global -Y) is written as material weight density rho = |w| / (A * 9.80665 m/s^2) with A the bare metal area pi/4 (OD^2 - ID^2); kgf/m3 equals kg/m3 numerically. Elements without a weight primitive have density 0.
Model members the SWBPIPE solve does not read (analysis_status, data_boundary, diagnostics, lines, unresolved_assumptions, constraints, equipment_interfaces, rule_pack_refs) are not exported.
